label: D1 after an unrewarded a1->S2 rare trial, stronger if the trial before was rewarded, fading late in the episode
short_terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * ep_trial
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (tv("action", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (tv("state", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * (tv("reward", -3) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == -1)
explanation: Feature is active only at D1, and almost only after the previous trial was a1 -> S2 (rare) and unrewarded (residual +0.34 there, about -0.03 after every other pattern; silent at GO/D2). Magnitude within that case is larger when the trial before was rewarded (two losses in a row give weak or no activation) and decreases with episode trial, going silent after about trial 80. The free fit adds that the trial-before being an a1 choice lowers it and having reached S1 raises it, plus a small effect of reward three trials back; belief_lo adds little. Large remaining misses are on the first trial of each window, where the previous trial falls outside the window so last_is cannot be computed. No future, hidden or model-output variables are used.

issues: Small caveat on wording: in the fitted short form, a1->S2 unrewarded after an unrewarded trial still predicts about 0.34 at trial 30, against about 0.63 when the trial before was rewarded (weights +0.55, +0.287, -0.007*ep_trial). So 'weaker' is accurate. The explanation's 'weak or no activation' overstates it a little, although some of the dev worst-fit windows (two losses in a row, actual 0, predicted about 0.39) do show zero.

Each term checks out on test. last_is('a1 S2 u') alone gives 0.335. Adding ep_trial raises it to 0.429, adding reward(-2)==1 instead gives 0.418, and all three give 0.488. Substitutes do worse: belief_lo 0.337 (or 0.435 with ep_trial), since_rev 0.391, belief_cover 0.402, state(-2)==S1 0.483, reward(-3) 0.393. So 'belief_lo adds little' holds, and the fading comes from episode time, not from time since reversal.

Misses on the short form show no large systematic error class. The worst windows are first-in-window trials (last_is cannot be computed), which the explanation already mentions, plus a few cases of two losses in a row. Mean error by phase is D1 -0.017, GO/D2 +0.008, and other D1 previous-trial cells are all about -0.025, which is just the timing baseline being absorbed.

The 'silent after trial ~80' claim is consistent with the timing baseline (D1 decile 8 is 0.0006, decile 9 is 0). Replacing the base term with an (ep_trial<80) gate scores the same (0.488), so the linear ep_trial term is a real description, not a fitted correction.
